program_overview.title: Competitive Programming Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: From your first contest to a rating you are proud of: C++ speed, the algorithmic arsenal, and the contest technique nobody teaches you alone.
program_overview.description:
Competitive programming is where algorithmic skill becomes fast, precise and fearless, and it pays off far beyond contests: the same technique wins placement rounds, quant interviews and hard engineering problems. This live online masterclass builds it in the order that actually works: C++ with STL and fast I/O, complexity instincts and the core structures, then the arsenal, number theory, combinatorics, tree and graph algorithms, dynamic programming from basics to bitmask and DP-on-trees, string algorithms, computational geometry, then the part solo learners never crack: contest strategy, speed, template discipline and reading problems under pressure, up through expert-level techniques like FFT and advanced graph theory. A finale month runs a full contest simulation and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of solving, with two more in hand. Problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.

faqs.question: What does this competitive programming course cover?
faqs.answer: The full competitive arsenal in order: C++ with STL and fast I/O, complexity, core structures, number theory, combinatorics and bit manipulation; then advanced dynamic programming, string algorithms, computational geometry, advanced data structures and contest strategy; then expert techniques, FFT and polynomial algorithms, linear algebra, advanced string structures and graph theory, with contest simulation throughout. A finale month runs a full contest and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn competitive programming properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Do I need to be good at maths for competitive programming?
faqs.answer: You need to be willing, not gifted. Competitive programming leans on discrete maths, number theory and combinatorics, and we teach every piece of it inside the course, in code, on problems. Plenty of strong competitors started shaky at maths; consistent solving is what builds the instinct.

faqs.question: Will you get me to a specific Codeforces rating?
faqs.answer: We will not promise a number, because rating depends on your own consistent practice and no honest teacher controls it. What we do is teach the technique, arsenal and contest craft that rating is built from, run real contests with honest debriefs, and give you the habits that keep the graph climbing after the course ends.
